display.title: Yud-Beis Tammuz: The Frierdiker Rebbe's Release from Prison
display.summary_short: Sixty years after the Frierdiker Rebbe was freed from a Soviet prison on Yud-Beis Tammuz, Uncle Yossi explains why the day is a celebration for every Jewish child.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given a few days before Yud-Beis Tammuz 5747. Uncle Yossi tells how, in 1927, the Frierdiker Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneerson, kept teaching Torah and mitzvos in Russia although the government forbade it, especially to young children. He was jailed and his life was in danger, while Jews everywhere prayed for him. By a miracle he was freed on the twelfth of Tammuz, his own birthday, and at once went back to founding yeshivos, shuls and mikvaos, bringing Yiddishkeit to tens of thousands. His victory was a victory for all of Klal Yisroel. Uncle Yossi adds that Tzivos Hashem grew out of the Frierdiker Rebbe's deep care for Jewish children, the leaders of tomorrow, and asks everyone to make strong resolutions to learn more Torah and do more mitzvos, praying that this redemption lead to the final Geulah with Moshiach.
display.lesson: The Frierdiker Rebbe risked his life so Jewish children could learn Torah; we celebrate by learning more Torah and doing more mitzvos.
